title: Warning Signs: Hazards, Road Users & Crossings
whatItIs: Triangular signs that warn you about people, animals and hazards ahead, from schoolchildren to level crossings.
keyFacts: Warning signs are triangles with a red border: slow down and look for the hazard shown.
Some school signs have amber lights that flash when children are crossing.
Level crossing signs warn you early: be ready to stop when the lights flash.
Animal signs mean animals may be on or near the road: slow down and give them room.
Pedestrian signs warn that people are likely to be in or crossing the road ahead.

visual.caption: Warnings about road users, animals and crossings

onTheTest.question: You see a warning sign showing two children. What does it warn you about?
options: Children going to or from school
A play street with no traffic
onTheTest.why: It's the 'children going to or from school' sign: expect children near the road and be ready to stop.

traps: At level crossings, don't mix up the gate symbol (barrier) with the train symbol (no barrier).
Animal signs show which animal to expect: wild animals, wild horses or horses with riders.
A warning sign tells you about a hazard; it doesn't give you priority or an order.
